title: Secure POST /users registration and login
summary: Added POST /users for user registration and login with bcrypt password hashing, parameterized SQLite queries, server-side input validation, generic auth failure messages, and session establishment on successful login.

threats_mitigated.description: Storing raw passwords in SQLite would expose credentials on database compromise.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: Hash passwords with bcrypt (12 rounds) before INSERT; only password_hash column is persisted.

threats_mitigated.description: Untrusted username/password concatenated into SQL could read or modify user records.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: All user lookups and inserts use parameterized queries with ? placeholders.

threats_mitigated.description: Distinct error messages for unknown vs wrong password reveal valid usernames.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: Login returns the same generic 'Invalid username or password' for missing users, missing hashes, and bad passwords.

threats_mitigated.threat_name: Password hash disclosure in API responses
threats_mitigated.description: Returning full user rows could leak password_hash to clients.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: serialize_user returns only id, username, and email; password fields are never included in JSON.

threats_mitigated.description: Oversized or malformed usernames, emails, and passwords could enable abuse or storage issues.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: Server-side allowlist validation for username pattern, email format, and minimum password length.

threats_mitigated.description: SQLite exceptions in responses could leak schema or query details.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: Catch sqlite3.Error and return generic JSON errors with correlation IDs; no SQL text in responses.

best_practices_achieved: bcrypt password hashing with configurable work factor
Parameterized SQL for all credential-related queries
Explicit public field projection via serialize_user
Security-relevant auth events logged without passwords
Flask signed session established on successful login
Incoming bcrypt dependency OSV-scanned clean at 4.2.1
Automated test coverage for registration, login, and conflict handling

secure_code_snippets.explanation: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt before persistence; INSERT uses parameterized SQL.
Login uses parameterized lookup and constant-time-safe generic failure responses.

guardrails_applied.title: Use modern password hashing and step-up MFA
guardrails_applied.instruction: Use Argon2id/bcrypt/scrypt with per-user salt and tuned work factors; require MFA for privileged actions.
guardrails_applied.notes: bcrypt with 12 rounds and per-hash salt via gensalt(); MFA out of scope for this demo endpoint.

guardrails_applied.title: Do not build queries or commands with string concatenation
guardrails_applied.instruction: Don't concatenate untrusted input into SQL/NoSQL/LDAP/OS command templates. Use parameterized APIs and safe query builders.
guardrails_applied.notes: Registration and login queries use ? parameter binding.

guardrails_applied.title: Validate and canonicalize all untrusted input server-side
guardrails_applied.instruction: Use allowlists, strict schemas, and length/type/range checks for all request data, file metadata, headers, and external API payloads.
guardrails_applied.notes: Username, email, password, and action fields validated server-side.

guardrails_applied.title: Do not return verbose internal errors to users
guardrails_applied.instruction: Don't expose stack traces, SQL errors, framework debug pages, or internal identifiers in responses. Return generic errors with correlation IDs.
guardrails_applied.notes: Database failures return generic messages with correlation_id.

guardrails_applied.title: Do not expose secrets in source, logs, or error messages
guardrails_applied.instruction: Don't hardcode credentials, include secrets in stack traces, or log tokens/keys/session IDs; load secrets from managed secret stores.
guardrails_applied.notes: Passwords and hashes are never logged or returned; SECRET_KEY loaded from environment with dev fallback documented.

guardrails_applied.title: Eliminate vulnerability classes structurally, not by case-by-case patching
guardrails_applied.instruction: For each class CISA highlights (SQLi, XSS, command injection, path traversal, memory-safety bugs), pick a structural mitigation rather than per-callsite review: parameterized queries / ORM-only DB access; auto-escaping templates (no raw HTML interpolation); a single command-runner that refuses string concatenation; a path-join helper that rejects '..'; memory-safe languages for new code. Lint/CI rules should fail builds that bypass these.
guardrails_applied.notes: Structural parameterized-query pattern used for all new credential paths.

guardrails_applied.title: Do not ship default, shared, or vendor-known passwords
guardrails_applied.instruction: Don't ship with default admin credentials, shared passwords across tenants, or known vendor backdoor accounts.
guardrails_applied.notes: Seed demo users have no password_hash; registration requires user-chosen passwords.

guardrails_applied.title: Log security-relevant events with integrity and retention controls
guardrails_applied.instruction: Log authentication, authorization failures, and admin actions with actor, target, outcome, and timestamp; protect logs from tampering.
guardrails_applied.notes: Registration, successful login, and failed login attempts logged without credential material.

guardrails_applied.title: Scan new dependencies against OSV.dev and auto-substitute safe versions
guardrails_applied.instruction: Before adding a package, scan name@version with OSV.dev and use a clean fixed version for HIGH/CRITICAL findings.
